Don't use `get_editor_by_name()`, the editors can be accessed directly.
Script editor has a singleton.
Shader editor could get one.
Assignment inside conditions is not allowed, per code style.

You can do `f->get_as_text().split("\n");`.

EDIT:
Looks like you already used that below...
This needs some proper name, even if `trash`.
This makes the class unused. Not sure if removing it is right, the current might break line endings (didn't test).
You can also do `code_edit->emit_signal(SceneStringName(text_changed))`.

I can't find anything about this here https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine/guidelines/cpp_usage_guidelines.html#disallowed-features. Does this fall under "Their use needs to serve a real purpose, such as improving code readability or performance"? Just want to confirm before I adjust my PRs.

Huh, I guess it was never documented.
But it's discouraged, because it negatively affects readability.
We generally discourage it indeed, it's just not very strictly enforced
To check `handles` I need the editor plugins which both don't have singletons, I will add those
It probably replaces other line endings like `\r\n` but we don't support those anyway.

Doing this resets the caret to the start of the file. It would be better to use `remove_text` and `insert_text` for each individual change instead.
Or save and restore the state with `CodeTextEditor::get_navigation_state()`, `set_edit_state()`.
This will crash if `code_text_editor` is null.
